internshipOverview.keyProjectsTasks: The main tasks included creating an information system and data flow diagram, preparing a Transaction Processing System (TPS) observation report, building a process flow diagram, developing an Excel-based Dynamic Pricing DSS model, comparing ERP, CRM, and SCM systems, and preparing reports based on Amazon’s information systems.
internshipOverview.skillsDeveloped: I improved my understanding of Management Information Systems and learned how different business systems work together. I also developed my Excel skills by using formulas such as SUMIF, practiced creating diagrams in draw.io, and improved my analytical and problem-solving skills through case studies and practical assignments.
internshipOverview.challengesFaced: One challenge was understanding how different information systems are connected in a large company like Amazon. Some concepts, such as ERP, SCM, and DSS, were new to me, so I reviewed the session materials and completed the practical exercises step by step to understand them better.
internshipOverview.achievements: I successfully completed the required assignments, including process diagrams, comparison reports, and the Excel-based DSS model. I also gained a clearer understanding of how information systems support business operations and decision-making in a real organization.

reflectionOnLearning.alignmentWithAcademicKnowledge: My studies at Samarkand International University of Technology gave me a basic understanding of information systems, business processes, and digital technologies. This knowledge made it easier to follow the internship sessions and understand the practical examples based on Amazon.
reflectionOnLearning.newKnowledgeGained: The internship introduced me to practical applications of information systems that were not covered in as much detail during my studies. I learned how Amazon uses TPS, ERP, CRM, SCM, cloud services, and decision support systems together to manage large-scale business operations and improve efficiency.
reflectionOnLearning.careerGoals: This internship increased my interest in Management Information Systems and digital business technologies. It showed me how information systems are used in real companies and encouraged me to continue developing my skills in this area.

feedbackForCompany.companySupport: The internship sessions were well organized, and our professor Shakhnawaz Ali explained the topics clearly. Learning materials, demonstrations, and practical assignments were provided, making it easier to understand the concepts and complete the required tasks.
feedbackForCompany.workEnvironment: Although the internship was conducted online through Google Meet, the learning environment was organized and professional. The sessions encouraged participation, and our professor was willing to answer questions and explain difficult topics.
feedbackForCompany.suggestionsForCompany: The internship could be improved by including more interactive activities, such as group discussions or additional real-life case studies. More time for questions and feedback after each practical task would also help students understand the topics more deeply.
feedbackForCompany.universityPreparation: The university provided a good theoretical foundation that helped me understand the internship content. However, including more practical exercises with business software and real company case studies during regular courses would prepare students even better.
feedbackForCompany.internshipCoordination: The internship was organized smoothly, and the schedule and learning activities were communicated clearly. Overall, the coordination between the university and the internship provider was effective.
feedbackForCompany.suggestionsForUniversity: The university could organize more internships with practical projects and industry professionals. It would also be useful to offer additional workshops on business software, data analysis tools, and information systems before internships begin.
feedbackForCompany.finalReport:
This internship gave me a practical introduction to how Management Information Systems are used in a large global company. Although the internship was conducted online through Google Meet, it included both theoretical explanations and practical activities that helped me connect classroom knowledge with real business situations. Amazon was used as the main case study, allowing me to understand how information systems support different business functions such as online shopping, logistics, customer service, inventory management, and decision-making.

During the internship, I completed several assignments, including an information system diagram, a business process flow diagram, a Transaction Processing System observation report, an enterprise systems comparison, and an Excel-based Decision Support System model. These activities helped me understand concepts such as TPS, ERP, CRM, SCM, and DSS in a more practical way. I also improved my Excel skills, learned to create process diagrams using draw.io, and became more confident in analyzing business processes.

Some topics were challenging at first because they involved systems used by large organizations that I had not studied in detail before. By reviewing the learning materials, following the demonstrations carefully, and completing each assignment step by step, I gradually understood how these systems work together.

One of the most valuable parts of the internship was seeing how information systems support real business decisions instead of only learning the theory behind them. It helped me understand the importance of data, technology, and business processes working together. Overall, this experience strengthened my interest in Management Information Systems and gave me a better understanding of how digital technologies are applied in modern organizations. I believe the knowledge and skills I gained during this internship will be useful in my future studies and career.

My role involved planning, coordinating, and monitoring recruitment activities while working closely with the marketing and admissions teams. I participated in planning promotional activities, coordinated communication between different departments, and contributed ideas for improving student engagement. I also assisted in evaluating the effectiveness of marketing campaigns by analyzing application and inquiry data and identifying opportunities for improvement.

Throughout the internship, I developed valuable professional skills, including project planning, teamwork, communication, leadership, problem-solving, and data analysis. Working with colleagues from different departments improved my ability to coordinate tasks, prioritize responsibilities, and make informed decisions under deadlines. One of the main challenges was maintaining student interest during recruitment campaigns. To overcome this challenge, our team reviewed previous campaign results, collected feedback from prospective students, and adjusted our promotional strategies to better meet their needs. This experience demonstrated the importance of flexibility, collaboration, and continuous improvement in project management.

Overall, the internship was an excellent learning experience that strengthened both my technical knowledge and professional skills. It helped me understand how project management contributes to organizational success and showed me the importance of strategic planning and data-driven decision-making. The experience confirmed my interest in pursuing a career in project management, business development, or digital transformation. I am grateful to EIT for providing a supportive environment where I was able to grow professionally and gain practical experience that will benefit my future career.

During my internship at the Samarkand Russian Theatre of Drama, I worked as a Technical Artist/Developer, supporting the theatre's creative and production teams by bridging technical implementation with visual and multimedia design. My role involved building small tools and workflows to support digital content used in productions, including projection assets, promotional media, and internal digital archiving of production materials.
My main tasks included preparing and optimizing image and video assets for use in stage projections and promotional materials, assisting with organizing and automating parts of the theatre's digital media library, and troubleshooting technical issues related to playback and display systems used during rehearsals and performances. I also contributed basic scripting to speed up repetitive tasks, such as batch-processing media files and standardizing formats across departments.
Throughout the internship, I developed practical skills in scripting and automation (Python), media file optimization, and cross-team communication — translating technical constraints into terms that non-technical staff, such as directors and stage designers, could easily understand. One of the main challenges I faced was adapting my computer science background, which is largely software- and systems-oriented, to the creative and often improvisational workflow of a theatre production. I addressed this by staying flexible, asking clarifying questions early, and iterating quickly based on feedback from the creative staff.
My coursework at Samarkand International University of Technology in software engineering, data structures, and basic graphics/media processing gave me a solid technical foundation for this work, particularly when handling media formats and building lightweight tools. However, the internship also exposed me to knowledge not covered in my academic program, such as the practical realities of live production environments, where reliability and simplicity of tools matter more than technical sophistication.
The theatre's staff were supportive and open to my suggestions, offering guidance where needed while also giving me the independence to solve problems on my own. The work environment was creative, collaborative, and distinct from a typical tech workplace, which was a valuable experience in itself.
Overall, this internship helped me see how computer science and technical skills can meaningfully support creative and cultural institutions, and it strengthened my interest in pursuing work at the intersection of technology and the arts going forward.///

During my internship at Asaka Bank, I worked in the customer service department, where my main task was issuing bank cards to customers. This involved verifying customer identification documents, entering personal and account information into the bank's internal system, and ensuring all paperwork was completed accurately and in compliance with bank regulations.
On a daily basis, I assisted numerous customers who came to apply for or collect their bank cards. I explained the necessary procedures to them, checked their documents, and processed their requests efficiently. I also helped organize and number physical documents to maintain proper records for auditing purposes.
Throughout the internship, I developed several important skills. My communication skills improved significantly as I interacted with a diverse range of customers daily. I also became more detail-oriented, since even small errors in documentation could cause serious issues in a banking environment. Additionally, I gained hands-on experience with the bank's internal software systems used for processing customer data.
One of the main challenges I faced was managing a high volume of customers during peak hours while maintaining accuracy in every transaction. To overcome this, I stayed organized, prioritized tasks effectively, and asked senior colleagues for advice whenever I was unsure about a procedure. Over time, I became faster and more confident in handling these situations independently.
My key achievements during this internship include successfully processing card issuance for a large number of customers without errors, improving my efficiency significantly by the end of the internship, and receiving positive feedback from my supervisor regarding my reliability, punctuality, and professionalism.
Overall, this internship gave me valuable real-world experience in the banking sector and strengthened my interest in pursuing a career in finance. It bridged the gap between my academic knowledge and practical banking operations, and I am grateful for the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals at Asaka Bank.
feedbackForCompany.finalComments: I am thankful for the opportunity to complete my internship at Asaka Bank. It was a valuable experience that helped me grow both professionally and personally, and I look forward to applying what I learned in my future career.

Although these problems delayed us for a while, we successfully completed the project in the end.

I also learned how important communication, proper planning, and staying calm under pressure are when working toward a deadline. Overall, this internship week was a valuable experience that strengthened both my technical knowledge and my ability to work effectively as part of a development team.

feedbackForCompany.finalReport:
The digital transformation of Central Asian higher education presents a unique opportunity for the Samarkand State Institute of Foreign Languages (SamSIFL) to extend its academic prestige beyond physical campus boundaries. Based on market research conducted during my internship, establishing a fully digital degree program—specifically a Bachelor of Arts in English Philology and Translation Studies—directly addresses critical accessibility gaps while diversifying the institute's revenue streams. Internal data revealed that a substantial portion of qualified applicants from distant regions drop out of the enrollment funnel due to relocation costs and limited housing. By removing these physical constraints, SamSIFL can democratize access for rural students and tap into a lucrative market of working professionals who require flexible, asynchronous schedules to balance their careers with skill upgrading.
Executing this launch successfully requires a targeted, phase-based marketing and operational strategy. The go-to-market plan focuses heavily on localized inbound digital campaigns, leveraging high-engagement channels like Telegram and Instagram to target ambitious young professionals and remote learners. To ensure financial viability and incentivize early adoption, the online degree should feature a value-based pricing model set slightly below traditional on-campus contracts, effectively passing institutional overhead savings directly to the students. This digital offering will be delivered via a mobile-optimized Learning Management System designed to function seamlessly even in low-bandwidth regions, ensuring that technical limitations do not hinder academic delivery.
While scalability is a primary benefit of this online model, preserving SamSIFL’s strict academic standards is paramount. Because asynchronous learning can naturally limit spontaneous spoken interaction, the curriculum design must mandate weekly, synchronous virtual conversation blocks capped at small peer groups to maintain oral fluency and rigorous assessment standards. Furthermore, dedicated digital admissions officers and a specialized technical support desk must be established to guide non-traditional students through the onboarding process and mitigate early tech fatigue. Ultimately, by capitalizing on these researched market demands and implementing structured quality guardrails, SamSIFL can future-proof its curriculum, capture a broader regional market share, and solidify its position as a modern leader in linguistic education.

What I Did During My Internship

During my internship as a Sales Store Manager, I gained valuable practical experience in retail management by participating in the daily operations of the store. My responsibilities included supporting the management team, supervising sales activities, assisting employees, monitoring inventory, and ensuring that customers received high-quality service. This experience allowed me to understand how different aspects of a retail business work together to achieve organizational goals.

One of my main responsibilities was assisting with the coordination of daily store operations. I helped organize employee schedules, delegated tasks when necessary, and monitored the progress of daily activities to ensure that work was completed efficiently. I also supported the sales team by encouraging effective communication with customers and promoting sales techniques such as upselling and cross-selling to improve store performance.

Inventory management was another important part of my internship. I monitored stock levels, participated in inventory checks, and worked with suppliers and warehouse staff to ensure that products were delivered on time. This helped me understand the importance of logistics and supply chain coordination in maintaining product availability and preventing stock shortages or overstocking.

Throughout the internship, I interacted with customers on a daily basis, assisting them with product selection, answering questions, and resolving complaints professionally. These experiences improved my communication and customer service skills while teaching me how to maintain customer satisfaction even in challenging situations.

During my internship, I also learned how managers analyze key performance indicators (KPIs), including sales revenue, conversion rate, and average transaction value. I observed how these indicators are used to evaluate store performance and support business decisions. In addition, I gained experience using point-of-sale (POS) systems and inventory management software to complete operational tasks and prepare reports.

internshipOverview.internshipRole: Logistics & Supply Chain Intern. I supported the company’s import and distribution operations end to end — from ordering goods from our Indonesian suppliers and following shipments through international transport and customs clearance, to preparing the related documentation and helping with a project to optimise delivery routes for our truck fleet. I also worked with the handling requirements for temperature-sensitive products.
internshipOverview.keyProjectsTasks:
During the internship I was involved across the company’s import and distribution operations. The main areas were:
– Procurement from our Indonesian suppliers — placing and following up on orders for the imported part of the catalogue (roughly half of our ~200 products).
– International transportation — following shipments on the ~2-month route from Indonesia to Uzbekistan and handling the issues that came up along the way.
– Customs clearance and documentation — preparing and checking the paperwork needed to clear goods, and working through inspections.
– A route-optimisation project for our delivery fleet — we run 100+ trucks, each delivering around 100 orders a day, so I helped analyse how to plan routes that reduce fuel costs and vehicle wear.
– Handling temperature-sensitive goods, which have to be kept in refrigerated storage and loaded only onto refrigerated trucks.
internshipOverview.skillsDeveloped: The internship helped me grow both technical and practical skills. On the technical side, I became much more comfortable with international trade documentation and the customs clearance process — reading and preparing the paperwork that goods need to cross borders — and I saw how route planning actually works when you’re organising a large fleet and thousands of deliveries a day. On the practical side, I got better at problem-solving under pressure, since a lot of what happened (border delays, inspections, rerouting) couldn’t be planned for and needed a quick workaround. I also improved at communicating with overseas suppliers and coordinating between everyone involved in a shipment — procurement, warehouse, drivers and customs.
internshipOverview.challengesFaced:
The hardest challenge was completely outside our control. We used to bring goods from Indonesia through Iran and Turkmenistan, but once the conflict involving Iran, the US and Israel began, that route was no longer an option and we had to reroute everything through China. China has strict transport rules and an enormous volume of exports, so the border crossings get heavily congested — our shipments would reach the border and then wait a long time before they could pass. It showed me how fast a supply chain has to adapt when the outside situation changes.

Customs was another challenge. Clearance here works on a random green/yellow/red system, and the inspector essentially decides which one a shipment gets. Green means it passes with almost no checks, yellow means an inspection, and red means a full, strict inspection. When we landed on yellow or red, clearing the goods took much longer and there were many details to resolve that we couldn’t predict in advance.

A third, more everyday challenge was the temperature-sensitive products. They have to stay cold, so they need refrigerated storage in the warehouse and can only go onto refrigerated trucks — if that isn’t managed properly, the goods are ruined. It made me pay close attention to how products are stored and loaded.
internshipOverview.achievements: As an intern I wasn’t running these processes on my own, but there are a few things I’m glad I was part of. I contributed to the route-optimisation project for our delivery fleet, which was aimed directly at cutting fuel costs and vehicle wear — being involved in something with a clear financial impact felt meaningful. I also helped keep shipments moving during the period when we had to reroute everything through China, which was a stressful stretch for the company. And by the end I could handle the customs documentation for a shipment largely on my own, which I definitely couldn’t have done at the start.

reflectionOnLearning.alignmentWithAcademicKnowledge: Several of my courses turned out to be directly relevant. Supply Chain Management gave me the overall picture of how the different stages connect, which helped me see where my daily tasks fit into the bigger process. Transportation & Distribution Management and Multimodal Transportation were especially useful once we had to move goods across several countries and switch routes — I already understood the basic logic of combining different transport modes and planning distribution. Warehouse Management helped me make sense of how goods are stored and organised, including the special handling that temperature-sensitive products need. Having that theoretical base meant I could follow what was happening around me fairly quickly instead of starting from zero.
reflectionOnLearning.newKnowledgeGained: Much of what I learned was the gap between how logistics looks in a textbook and how it works in reality. In class you learn the “right” way to plan a route or clear customs; in practice, so much depends on things you can’t control — a random customs inspection, a conflict that closes a route almost overnight, a border too congested to move through quickly. I hadn’t realised how directly geopolitics shapes everyday logistics until I watched us redesign our whole import route because of the war. I also picked up the practical side of cold-chain handling and saw how much documentation sits behind a single international shipment — far more than I’d expected.
reflectionOnLearning.careerGoals: This internship confirmed the direction I already wanted to take. I want to work as a logistics specialist in international logistics — moving cargo between countries — and being involved in buying goods from foreign partners and following a shipment all the way from Indonesia to Uzbekistan through several countries showed me that this is exactly the kind of work I find interesting. Seeing the real challenges up close made me more sure about it, not less.

feedbackForCompany.companySupport: The company was supportive throughout. My mentor was the HR Manager, who guided me, answered my questions and made sure I actually understood what was going on rather than just leaving me to watch. Everyone I worked with was willing to explain things when I asked, even though they were all busy with their own tasks. I always had access to the information and people I needed to learn from the work, which made a big difference.
feedbackForCompany.workEnvironment: The work environment was professional and calm, but not slow — everyone was clearly busy and focused, and nobody was just sitting around. At the same time the atmosphere was friendly and easy to be part of, so it never felt tense or unwelcoming. I liked that combination: people took their work seriously and got things done, but they were still approachable and happy to help an intern find their feet.
feedbackForCompany.suggestionsForCompany: If I could suggest anything, it would come from the problems we faced during my time there. First, having a clearer backup plan for transport routes could help — when the situation with Iran forced us to reroute everything through China, a lot had to be figured out under pressure, and pre-arranged alternative routes and partners might soften that kind of shock next time. Second, since a share of our goods are temperature-sensitive, tighter monitoring of the cold chain during storage and loading would reduce the risk of spoilage. Beyond that, the internship itself was well run, so these are small additions rather than real complaints.
feedbackForCompany.universityPreparation: On the theory side the university prepared me reasonably well — the logistics and supply chain courses gave me a solid foundation that I could actually use. Where I think it could improve is on the practical side. A lot of what I ran into during the internship — real customs documentation, the random inspection system, sudden route changes because of outside events — isn’t really covered in class, and I learned it entirely on the job. More hands-on work, real case studies and exposure to how the paperwork and disruptions actually look would help students step into an internship better prepared.
feedbackForCompany.internshipCoordination: Honestly, there wasn’t any coordination between the university and the company during my internship. I found the company myself and arranged and carried out the whole placement on my own, without the university being involved. So I can’t really say the coordination was effective or not — it simply didn’t happen in my case, and that’s the main area I’d point to for improvement.
feedbackForCompany.suggestionsForUniversity: My main suggestion is for the university to take a more active role in internships. In my case I did everything myself — finding the company, arranging the placement and managing it — and it would help a lot if the university built partnerships with companies, kept some contact during the internship and assigned a supervisor students could turn to. Even a small amount of coordination and a list of partner companies would make the whole process less stressful and give students access to opportunities they might not find on their own.
feedbackForCompany.finalReport:
During my internship at LLC ARGOS, a distribution company based in Uzbekistan, I worked as a Logistics & Supply Chain Intern for two months, from 1 May to 1 July. The company distributes around 200 different products to retail and wholesale stores, hotels, restaurants and cafés, and imports roughly half of its catalogue from Indonesia — a journey that takes about two months from supplier to warehouse. My time there gave me a close look at almost every stage of that process.

My work covered several main areas. The first was procurement: I was involved in ordering goods from our Indonesian suppliers and following those orders through. The second was international transportation, where I helped track shipments on their long route to Uzbekistan and dealt with the problems that came up along the way. The third was customs clearance and documentation, which turned out to be one of the most detailed and demanding parts of the job. The fourth was a project to optimise delivery routes for our fleet of more than 100 trucks — each delivering around 100 orders a day — with the goal of reducing fuel costs and wear on the vehicles. I also worked with the handling of temperature-sensitive goods, which need refrigerated storage and refrigerated trucks to avoid spoiling.

The internship fell during a difficult period. Because of the conflict involving Iran, the US and Israel, we could no longer move goods through Iran and Turkmenistan and had to reroute everything through China. China’s strict transport rules and huge export volume meant serious congestion at the borders, and shipments often reached the crossing only to wait a long time before they could pass. Customs added its own uncertainty — the random green/yellow/red inspection system meant any shipment could be pulled for a full check.

Working through these problems taught me more than any single task could. I learned how quickly a supply chain has to adapt to events far outside a company’s control, how much documentation sits behind international trade, and how route planning really works once real constraints get in the way of the ideal answer. Overall, the internship connected what I’ve studied in International Logistics to the realities of the field and confirmed that international logistics is where I want to build my career.

Overall Rating: 5 (Great)

Overall this was an excellent experience. I’m grateful I got to be part of real operations during such an unusual period, and it gave me a much clearer idea of the career I want to pursue.

feedbackForCompany.finalReport:
**Internship Activities**

During my one-month internship in the IT Department at UZEX, I gained practical experience in cybersecurity, enterprise network architecture, and information security management. From my very first day, I actively communicated with cybersecurity specialists, asking questions to gain a thorough understanding of how the organization's infrastructure is designed, protected, and maintained. This proactive approach helped me bridge the gap between the theoretical knowledge I acquired at Samarkand International University of Technology (SIUT) and real-world cybersecurity practices.

One of my primary responsibilities was studying the organization's internal network architecture. I learned how the enterprise network is isolated from direct Internet access through network segmentation, significantly reducing the risk of external cyberattacks. I also observed how every workstation is assigned a static IP address, allowing administrators to accurately identify user activities, investigate security incidents, and maintain accountability through detailed audit logs. This experience demonstrated the importance of access control, user authentication, and continuous monitoring in protecting critical organizational resources.

To reinforce my understanding, I recreated parts of the organization's network using Cisco Packet Tracer. By simulating routers, switches, and end-user devices, I gained a deeper understanding of enterprise network design, communication between network components, and the implementation of secure network architectures.

Another important aspect of my internship was analyzing cybersecurity from an attacker's perspective. I evaluated how both external attackers and insider threats could exploit vulnerabilities within an organization. In particular, I examined scenarios in which brokers might attempt to bypass organizational policies by installing unauthorized software or using prohibited applications to gain an unfair advantage. This analysis emphasized the importance of endpoint protection, application control, security policies, and continuous monitoring in preventing insider misuse and maintaining the integrity of organizational systems.

I also learned how the IT department centrally manages and secures employee workstations. If suspicious activity or a potential security incident is detected, IT specialists can remotely monitor a user's screen and, when necessary, take control of the workstation to investigate and resolve the issue. This capability enables a rapid response to security incidents, minimizes potential risks, and ensures compliance with organizational security policies across the enterprise.

Due to the organization's strict security regulations, I was not permitted to use tools such as Wireshark on the production network. Although this limited direct packet analysis, it reinforced the importance of protecting sensitive environments and following established security procedures when working with critical infrastructure.

In addition to cybersecurity activities, I completed professional training on exchange trading to better understand the organization's core business processes. I studied the official training materials, learned how electronic trading is conducted within UZEX, and successfully passed the professional certification examination required for brokers. As a result, I became a certified UZEX trader. Understanding both the technical infrastructure and business operations gave me valuable insight into how cybersecurity supports secure, transparent, and reliable trading.

Overall, this internship significantly expanded my practical knowledge of enterprise cybersecurity, network security, organizational risk management, and secure system administration. It strengthened my analytical thinking, exposed me to professional cybersecurity practices that are difficult to experience in a classroom environment, and confirmed my aspiration to pursue a career in cybersecurity.

feedbackForCompany.finalReport: During my industrial internship within the Supply Chain and Logistics Department at the Coca-Cola plant, I actively participated in optimizing distribution workflows. My responsibilities were centered on managing the distribution network and coordinating the delivery of finished goods from the production plant to the city’s major transportation hubs: the central railway station and the international airport. My day-to-day tasks involved monitoring daily dispatch volumes from the plant's warehouses, analyzing real-time inventory levels at retail outlets within the station and airport, and calculating the optimal fleet capacity required for transport. One of the main challenges I faced during the internship was handling vehicle delays at the strict security checkpoints of the airport and railway infrastructure. To minimize these operational bottlenecks, I conducted a thorough time-motion study of our delivery routes and proposed a restructured delivery schedule. We shifted the "unloading windows" to off-peak hours when checkpoint congestion is minimal. Additionally, working alongside the plant's legal team, we streamlined the pre-submission workflow for security documentation to secure long-term vehicle permits. Implementing these optimized delivery schedules successfully reduced average truck idle time at secure checkpoints by 15%, significantly enhancing overall fleet utilization efficiency. Furthermore, throughout the entire duration of my internship, we maintained a zero-incident record for out-of-stock items at both transit hubs, completely satisfying consumer demand during peak travel periods. This internship allowed me to seamlessly apply the theoretical knowledge gained at Samarkand International University of Technology (SIUT) to a real-world, large-scale manufacturing environment. I gained deep insights into route optimization, freight documentation, and operational compliance within highly secured infrastructure facilities. Ultimately, this practical experience has validated my career aspirations and established a solid foundation for my future growth in the field of Supply Chain Management.

feedbackForCompany.finalReport:
Introduction
This report provides a comprehensive overview of my internship at Gelion Factory in Samarkand, a prominent producer of bottled water and soft beverages in Uzbekistan. I was placed in the Accounting Department for [X] weeks as part of the SIUT internship program. The primary objectives were to apply theoretical accounting knowledge to a real-world manufacturing environment, develop practical skills in production cost accounting and tax compliance, and gain exposure to the daily operations of a large-scale factory.
Company Background
Gelion Factory operates a modern production facility in Samarkand city, manufacturing a diverse range of products including purified drinking water, carbonated drinks, and fruit juices. The company manages a complex supply chain involving both local and imported raw materials – such as PET preforms, bottle caps, labels, flavor concentrates, and sweeteners – alongside large-scale production machinery and a widespread distribution network across Uzbekistan. The Accounting Department is responsible for cost tracking, supplier payments, inventory valuation, tax reporting (VAT and excise), payroll, and monthly/quarterly financial closing.
Daily Responsibilities and Key Tasks
Throughout my internship, I was actively engaged in a variety of accounting functions under the direct supervision of a senior accountant and the Chief Accountant.

Invoice Processing and Accounts Payable: I processed incoming supplier invoices for raw materials including PET bottles, labels, packaging films, and beverage concentrates. I verified each invoice against delivery notes and purchase orders, identified and resolved discrepancies with the procurement team, and entered approved transactions into the 1C:Accounting system.
 Skills and Knowledge Gained

This internship significantly enhanced my practical accounting abilities. I gained hands-on proficiency in 1C:Accounting software, deepened my understanding of production cost allocation, and learned Uzbek excise tax procedures in detail. I also developed strong Excel skills (pivot tables, VLOOKUPs, SUMIFS), improved my attention to detail, and learned to work effectively under tight month-end deadlines. Equally important, I gained a holistic understanding of how the accounting department interacts with procurement, warehouse, and production teams – a perspective never fully captured in university lectures.
Conclusion and Career Impact

This internship was an invaluable experience that transformed my theoretical accounting knowledge into practical, workplace-ready competence.
